definition: A bed of sorbent that takes up a gas or solute and is regenerated by a pressure, vacuum or temperature swing.
A plant that separates air into oxygen, nitrogen and argon, cryogenically or by membrane.
A vessel in which bacteria break down organic matter without oxygen, producing biogas.
A furnace that reheats formed steel or metal to relieve stress and restore ductility.
An electric arc heating a gas stream directly.
A reformer that partially oxidizes the feed with oxygen to supply the reforming heat inside one vessel.
A converter that blows oxygen through hot metal and scrap to make steel.
A cementitious material that replaces or dilutes clinker in cement.
A coke-fired counter-current shaft that reduces iron ore to hot metal.
A fired or electric vessel that raises steam or hot water for use elsewhere on site.
A kiln-like unit that heats a solid to drive off CO2 or water (limestone, alumina, clays).
A plant that separates CO2 from a gas stream or from air.
A machine that solidifies liquid metal into slabs, billets, strip or ingots.
A refrigeration machine producing chilled water, cold air or process cooling.
Clean-in-place and washing systems in food and drink plants.
The grate or planetary cooler that quenches clinker leaving a cement kiln.
A continuous line that galvanizes, tins or otherwise coats steel strip.
A battery of ovens that carbonizes coal into coke.
A gas turbine whose exhaust raises steam for a steam turbine; with heat taken off, a CHP unit.
A gas turbine or gas engine producing shaft power or electricity.
A machine that raises the pressure of a gas: air, process gas, CO2 or natural gas.
A vessel that blows air or oxygen through a molten matte or metal to refine it.
A belt or similar system moving bulk material.
A tower that rejects heat to air by evaporation or dry cooling.
A machine that breaks rock or ore to a smaller size before grinding.
A drum or ring machine stripping bark from logs, usually with a chipper.
A pressure vessel that cooks wood chips (pulp) or bauxite (Bayer alumina) with chemicals and heat.
A fired or electric heater that heats a process stream or air directly, without a working fluid.
A column separating liquids by boiling point, with its reboiler and condenser.
A whole distilling plant producing beverage spirits (mashing, fermentation, distillation).
A rig and its power supply drilling oil, gas or geothermal wells.
A unit that removes water from a solid product by heat or airflow.
A furnace melting or smelting a charge with electric arcs from graphite electrodes.
A cell reducing or separating a product electrochemically: aluminium, chlor-alkali, electrowinning.
A stack that splits water into hydrogen and oxygen.
A unit that concentrates a liquor or brine by boiling off water.
A fan or blower moving air or gas, and the system it serves.
A vessel in which microorganisms convert a feedstock to a product such as ethanol.
A burner that destroys waste or vented gas by combustion.
A cell separating minerals by attaching them to air bubbles.
The pumps and power units that hydraulically fracture a well.
A cell converting a fuel's chemical energy to electricity without combustion.
A fired or electric enclosure heating a solid charge: reheating, heat treatment, glass melting, anode baking.
A plant removing acid gases, sulphur or water from natural gas or process gas.
A reactor converting a solid or liquid feed to syngas by partial oxidation.
A well producing geothermal heat.
A mill reducing a solid to powder: ball, SAG, vertical roller, high-pressure rolls.
An off-road truck hauling ore or overburden at a mine.
An exchanger heating a product with steam or hot water: kettles, retorts, plate exchangers.
A machine that lifts heat from a low-temperature source to a useful temperature.
Equipment recovering heat from an exhaust, product or effluent for reuse.
A winder raising ore and people in a mine shaft.
A unit heater or make-up air heater warming a building (HVAC heating).
A plant burning waste with energy recovery and flue-gas cleaning.
A coil heating a conductive workpiece or melt by induced currents.
A rotary, shaft or tunnel kiln firing a solid at high temperature: clinker, lime, ceramics, lumber.
A vessel, heap or in-situ system dissolving metal from ore.
Luminaires and their controls.
A plant liquefying natural gas or hydrogen.
An organizational measure rather than a device: energy management, leak detection, monitoring.
A furnace melting metal or glass: cupola, reverberatory, induction, electric melter.
A small gas turbine, typically under 1 MW.
A heater using microwave, ohmic or infrared energy.
A whole mine treated as one plant: extraction, haulage, ventilation, hoisting and dewatering together.
Off-road vehicles and mobile machinery at a site.
An electric motor and its drive.
The do-nothing option on an abatement node: no equipment, no cost and no energy use.
An enclosed chamber baking, roasting or curing a product.
The forming and press sections of a paper machine.
A plant preparing carbon paste for Soderberg electrodes.
A heat exchanger that pasteurizes a liquid product.
A plant forming pellets: induration-fired iron ore pellets, or pressed biomass fuel pellets.
A heater using light-driven chemistry.
Solar photovoltaic panels, with any storage they carry.
A line removing scale from steel strip in acid.
A pipeline transporting a fluid, with its compression or pumping.
An electric arc or plasma torch heating a gas or charge to very high temperature.
A gas- or air-driven controller, actuator or pump at a well site or facility.
The fired vessel before a cement kiln where most calcination happens.
A burner or heater warming a vessel or charge before use, such as a ladle.
A press dewatering, forming or moulding a product.
A change to a process, feedstock or practice that is not a device.
A refiner or pulper turning wood chips or recovered paper into fibre.
A pump and the system it serves.
A heater using radio-frequency or microwave energy.
A vessel in which a chemical or nuclear reaction takes place.
A piston engine driving a generator, pump or compressor.
A whole refinery treated as one plant: a petroleum refinery, or a Bayer alumina refinery.
A furnace refining molten metal.
A heater passing current through a resistive element.
A furnace or oven roasting a solid.
A mill reducing the thickness of metal between rolls, hot or cold.
A rotating machine heating a gas by compression.
Equipment separating phases or particles: thickeners, clarifiers, membranes, sorters, froth treatment.
A shaft reducing iron ore directly with gas below the melting point.
A strand agglomerating iron ore fines into sinter.
A vessel reducing ore to liquid metal in a molten bath.
Non-concentrating solar thermal collectors.
Mirrors concentrating sunlight to raise high-temperature heat.
Furnaces cracking hydrocarbons to olefins with steam, and their cold end.
A fired reformer producing syngas or hydrogen from methane and steam.
A turbine expanding steam to produce shaft power or electricity.
An underground cavern (solution-mined salt or lined rock) storing compressed gas.
An energy store charged with heat or electricity and discharged as steam or hot gas.
A reactor converting oils and fats to biodiesel.
A turbine recovering work from an expanding gas.
A unit curing coatings with ultraviolet or infrared light.
A pressure-regulating or throttling valve; at a gas let-down station, with the line heater that offsets its Joule-Thomson cooling.
A compressor raising the pressure of vapour so its latent heat can be reused.
A ventilation system and its controls.
A well injecting or producing fluids.
A wind turbine generating electricity at a site.
A whole pulp mill treated as one plant: wood handling, pulping, bleaching, chemical recovery, and utilities.
